title: Runtime N operates on separate Development N+1 and never mutates itself
rationale: Separate clones and object stores keep the executable identity a Run trusts distinct from the repository under active development, so self-development cannot silently change the code executing it.

title: Push and Runtime promotion remain maintainer-owned, never automatic
rationale: WFC coordinates only its admitted committed envelope; the maintainer separately reviews, accepts, may push, and may later promote a Runtime, so widening execution authority always requires an explicit human act.

title: Policy determines authority; Profile determines flow; WorkItem bounds task/scope; Coordinator executes deterministically; Agent performs bounded work
rationale: Separating what is allowed (Policy), how work flows (Profile), what is in scope (WorkItem), what executes it (Coordinator), and who performs semantic work (Agent) keeps authority independent of any single agent's self-report.

title: WFC is Level-0 governed bounded execution, not Level-1 project planning or orchestration
rationale: Real DMC work against Core falsified the earlier fractal (self-similar nested loop) hypothesis: Level 0 converges a known, pinned WorkItem, while Level 1 (goal custody, discovery, replanning, cross-session persistence) is unpinned and discovery-driven. WFC intentionally owns only Level 0.

title: Agent requests and self-report do not themselves grant repository authority
rationale: Git and reducer-enforced admitted routes are authority; an agent's requested route, proposed Finding disposition, or scope request is a request the Coordinator may reject. Dogfooding repeatedly exercised this and the reducer held fail-closed every time.

title: Trusted evidence execution is Coordinator-owned; agent-side checks are exploratory only
rationale: Only Coordinator-selected, pinned evidence commands are trusted repository truth; an agent's own shell checks (e.g. a missing bare `python`) are informative to the agent but never substitute for or override trusted evidence.

title: Coordinator hard autonomous-Hop ceiling is independent of WorkItem and RepositoryPolicy budgets
rationale: WorkItem.max_autonomous_hops <= RepositoryPolicy.max_autonomous_hops <= Coordinator hard ceiling is enforced independently at four separate sites (RepositoryPolicy parsing, WorkItem admission, operator preflight, serial-Hop driver), so raising the product ceiling never widens any configured policy or WorkItem by itself.

title: Coordinator hard autonomous-Hop ceiling is currently 20
rationale: Raised from a historical value of 5 (dcb1da0, accepted 9fc478b) to decouple the product ceiling from that coincidentally-equal old value. This repository's own self-development RepositoryPolicy deliberately keeps max_autonomous_hops at 5; the higher ceiling is not itself an authorization to run longer Hop budgets.

title: Provider sandboxing is not claimed as Coordinator-owned containment
rationale: The Codex CLI adapter's `--sandbox workspace-write` request is provider-owned behavior the Coordinator does not verify; treating it as a trusted OS/environment boundary would overclaim a guarantee WFC does not currently provide.

title: WFC Project Memory promotion moves toward a Git-backed review boundary rather than adding locking/transactional exclusivity to the custom staging protocol
rationale: The strong staged-proposal/fingerprint protocol (d201af5) closed the semantic and Make-ordering findings from the first review, but the correction rereview (773ea97) showed its marker-load/compare/write/consume sequence is not an exclusive critical section: two concurrent `memory-promote` processes can both validate and consume one reviewed proposal (14-of-30 double-success). Closing that would require locking, atomic marker claim, or equivalent exclusive-consumption machinery. Concurrent/multi-user promotion is not a current requirement -- Project Memory is maintained by a single maintainer, and uncoordinated simultaneous workbook editing would already need coordination outside memory-promote -- so further transactional machinery is disproportionate. The experiment showed that a strong staged proposal/approval contract naturally grows a second state/identity lifecycle beside Git; WFC will instead simplify toward two persistent representations only (canonical JSON, editable ODS), with Git itself as the proposal/review/acceptance/history/rollback boundary and at most a non-persistent temporary import buffer carrying no proposal identity, approval semantics, fingerprint lifecycle, or lock. The strong-staging implementation and its reviews remain in Git history as evidence for a future use case that genuinely needs multi-user delayed-approval promotion. The simplification was subsequently implemented (871ab14) and independently reviewed (9b9e99e, 2026-09-28): the Git-backed contract was found correctly implemented for the documented serial maintainer flow, with acceptance withheld only for one MINOR finding -- the blanket `make -j` parallel-safety claim in `Makefile` and `project_memory/README.adoc` is false for memory targets that share the workbook or canonical JSON.

title: Projected result contracts ship as permanent slices P1-P5, each needing its own Commission
rationale: A class of mechanical contract failures is removed by making inadmissible result shapes inexpressible at the agent boundary rather than only rejected afterwards, sequenced as small permanent slices with Runtime promotion points between them. P1 (selection seam, persisted ResultContractKind/version sibling pair) and P2 (distinct WorkResult/ReviewVerdict families) are implemented, independently accepted, and contained in the Runtime at 0ab2063. P3 (Finding authorship/update projection) has passed out of the concept/design stage: it has a maintainer-accepted design record and a committed Commission (d2adf08) which authorized the one real Run that has already executed and stopped on a typed scope escalation, so P3 is authorized-but-incomplete rather than unauthorized, and any continuation requires a fresh successor Commission. P3.5 (Commission/authority composition conformance), P4 (Coordinator-owned effects including canonical CommitIntent rendering) and P5 (provider capability cleanup) remain concept/design only and authorize nothing; the roadmap revision that added P3.5 was independently reviewed and closed (c8c9736, f31a423, 5979d75). The three non-P1 failure classes must stay visible as distinct: what one invocation may express (P2/P3), whether individually valid phase capabilities compose into a mechanically completable workflow (P3.5), and model-authored restatement of facts the Coordinator already knows deterministically (P4). Projection narrows vocabulary; it never narrows or replaces reducer authority. Subsequent planning disposition (2026-10-26, not part of the original 2026-10-08 delivery chronology above and not a revision of it): two independent reassessments (WI-WFC-P35-STRUCTURAL-INVARIANT-REASSESSMENT-001, accepted H004 commit fab606e; WI-WFC-P35-REQUIREMENTS-ARCHAEOLOGY-REASSESSMENT-001, accepted H004 commit e5af5c8f) each independently escalated the P3.5 universal-versus-existential requirements choice rather than resolving it. The maintainer has since selected the narrower existential authority/state-aware reachability predicate as the intended future P3.5 direction (DEC-WFC-018) and separately decided to prioritize Front Door, including a Runtime/Profile/Commission boundary refactor, ahead of further P3.5 implementation (DEC-WFC-017). P3.5 remains concept/design-only and unimplemented; this does not retroactively change the 2026-10-08 sequencing decision recorded above.

title: Coordinator-required evidence belongs only on a gate-review phase carrying an explicit failed_evidence_route
rationale: A worker or correction phase cannot route a trusted-evidence failure, so required evidence placed on one converts an ordinary failure into a terminal stop and invites the agent to treat downstream acceptance evidence as its own completion prerequisite. Production preflight now refuses a profile whose non-gate phase declares required evidence and refuses a required-evidence gate with no failed_evidence_route (operator.py:130, :134), and profile parsing refuses failed_evidence_route outside a gate review (serialization.py:573). Empirical basis: three non-accepting P2 Runs localized by the stagnation audit to exactly this topology, and the P3 Commission's second provider-free PREPARE refusal. Semantic review acceptance never substitutes for Coordinator-owned trusted evidence; the canonical converging topology is worker(no evidence) -> gate(evidence, failed_evidence_route) -> correction(no evidence) -> rereview gate(evidence, failed_evidence_route).

title: Salvage preserves work, not authority; an unclean Run or Hop resolves into one of four maintainer-chosen outcomes
rationale: Repeated real cases produced a stable procedure, now canonical and listed in the authority index. A Run or Hop that does not cleanly complete resolves into exactly one maintainer-chosen outcome -- same-Run reconcile/resume, maintainer salvage plus a fresh successor Run, forensic preservation only, or discard -- and the Coordinator derives at most the bounded facts that make an outcome eligible, never the choice. Salvage freezes state before mutating history, preserves exactly the attributable candidate paths without content repair under an explicitly non-authoritative subject, and verifies `salvage commit delta == frozen dirty candidate delta`. A salvage commit is durable provenance and preserved work; it is never a retroactively successful Hop, a trusted commit, trusted evidence, review, acceptance, Finding disposition, a scope grant, Runtime promotion, or authority for a successor. An execution starting point is not an assurance baseline, and salvage ancestry grants no correctness or review credit.

title: Semantic successor continuation is a fresh separately authorized Run, never resume, retry, or replay
rationale: A legitimate scope-escalation predecessor finishes awaiting_human, which is terminal for autonomous dispatch: its admitted governing inputs, identity, state, Hops, Findings and trusted evidence stay frozen and are never mutated to retrofit continuation. A correlated worker escalation is copied into an immutable SemanticStop record before the reducer selects the controlling mechanical stop_reason, so a later dirty-state or CommitIntent preemption cannot obscure the answerable semantic question; stop_reason remains the controlling reduction reason and anomalies remain mechanical diagnostics. The successor is a new WorkItem and Run with backward-only SuccessorProvenance linkage, and must state explicitly that it is fresh -- resume would treat unreviewed predecessor state as accepted, retry would imply the predecessor authority sufficed, replay would imply its actions should be reproduced, and none is true when the predecessor was correctly insufficient in authority. This mechanism is deliberately distinct from FTR-WFC-ATOMIC-HOP-RECOVERY's same-Run technical reconcile/resume. Provenance and current status: the design's independent architecture review (2026-09-30) judged the central architecture right -- semantic observation orthogonal to mechanical control, awaiting_human terminal rather than same-Run suspension, predecessor truth backward-linked rather than back-patched, salvage optional and non-authoritative -- while returning CHANGES_REQUIRED on two bounded persistence/trust gaps, closed by the design lineage's H003 correction, after which implementation was commissioned. The semantics recorded here are current: they are implemented in source and restated in the authoritative successor-continuation runbook. No separate post-H003 design re-acceptance artifact exists, and the acceptance of the resulting operator implementation is a separate, still-open question tracked by CONC-WFC-ATOMIC-HOP-RECOVERY-WIRING.

title: A terminal Level-0 stop terminates that Run, not the enclosing Level-1 body of work
rationale: Hop outcome, Run outcome and WorkItem completion are three different altitudes and must not be collapsed. A Hop that reports accurately that its granted authority is insufficient has completed its own bounded responsibility; the Run then has a correct durable non-success disposition; the WorkItem can remain open across however many Runs it eventually takes. `awaiting_human` is primarily a statement about the stopped Run's own authority and declared mechanics, not a product-level claim that the next actor must be a human. A surrounding layer may disposition a stop only within authority it already holds and must otherwise propagate it upward to the next authority-bearing layer, ultimately a human; catching a stop must never become self-authorized scope or authority expansion. Calling a correct escalation a half Hop or an implementation failure would train operators and agents to hide exactly the behavior the trust boundary exists to produce.

title: Harness v0 is deterministic operator mechanics and owns no semantic content
rationale: Repeated hand-authored PREPARE/LAUNCH shell blocks were a real source of substrate mistakes, so the established deterministic preparation contract was mechanized as repository-owned `scripts/wfc_op.py` (prepare, launch, status, archive), living in Development outside the `workflow_coordinator` package. It pins exact Development/Runtime/Evidence identities, enforces the self-development preconditions, writes execution-bindings.yaml from explicit --role-binding inputs only, assembles and verifies the controlled PATH, runs the pinned Runtime's own provider-free preflight, and stops at PREPARED / NOT LAUNCHED with STATE still absent. It deliberately does not choose the next WorkItem, estimate difficulty, choose semantic execution strategy, decompose tasks, author Commissions, select a model semantically, curate the semantic ledger, promote Runtime, push, repair failed Runs, or reinterpret terminal Run state. Those belong to the maintainer-occupied tier above it. OPS exists once prepare succeeds; STATE is created only when launch actually starts a Run, and confusing prepared with launched is the most common misreading of the system.

title: Front Door, including the Runtime/Profile/Commission boundary refactor, is prioritized ahead of further P3.5 implementation
rationale: P3.5 static validation should target a coherent, stable workflow-program model. Implementing it now against commission-specific duplicated profiles risks cementing precisely the structure that needs to change: the accepted P3.5 design's own 43/0 legacy-profile rejection result is partly a symptom of per-Commission profile duplication (45 profiles independently measured to reduce to one repeated logical cycle across 35 of 36 profiles in the amendment baseline, per the Commissioning concept and the 2026-10-25 Front Door Stage 1 Commission test-burden finding), not only of the validator's strictness. This decision does not revoke current runtime safety guards, accepted evidence, or the open BUG-WFC-SELF-DEVELOPMENT-GATE-FINDING-AUTHORITY, and it does not authorize any Profile/Commission implementation by itself; it is independently corroborated by the workflow-coordinator-run-evidence Run Ledger's P3.5 Requirements-Archaeology Reassessment entry (2026-10-26), which records the same prioritization as supplied planning context rather than a Run outcome.

title: The existential authority/state-aware reachability predicate is selected as the intended future P3.5 requirements direction
rationale: The accepted P3.5 design formalizes a universal path condition (every relevant checkpoint-reaching continuation of an opener-capable phase must encounter a strictly later disposer). Two independent 2026-10-25/26 reassessments each found the original Concept's own first written revision (965d14d) already internally inconsistent -- containing both the universal wording and a conflicting existential-looking boundary sentence -- and each escalated the choice between a universal and an existential (authority/state-aware reachability) predicate to the maintainer rather than resolving it. The maintainer selects the narrower existential predicate: for a newly opened blocking Finding, at least one actually selectable, legally authorized route sequence must reach a suitable disposition opportunity in a later invocation; for a carried open Finding, the current phase may itself be a legal disposer, or one may be reachable later. This does not imply an agent will choose the repair route or successfully dispose the Finding, and it does not relax the existing dynamic reducer completion guard, which independently rejects a direct completion attempt made with an open blocker. This decision selects a requirements direction only; it does not authorize a P3.5 implementation Commission, which remains separately gated behind DEC-WFC-017's Front Door prioritization.

title: Front Door Basic, not Advanced, is the Level-0 MVP target; mechanical effort minimization excludes professional task/scope/acceptance authoring
rationale: The maintainer's priority is a Level-0 product reached soon through legible mechanics, not a new semantic authoring capability. A human may continue to prepare the professional task interactively with an LLM exactly as today; Front Door's purpose is to make Commission creation, preparation, admission, execution, and archiving as simple and legible as possible. The professional effort of writing the task description, scope, and acceptance criteria is explicitly excluded from the mechanical effort this milestone minimizes. This narrows emphasis within the existing MVP concept thesis and the 2026-10-21 record's Stage 1 framing; it does not redefine either, and it authorizes no implementation.

title: Front Door Basic's human and machine interfaces share one structured, validatable semantic Commission contract with a deterministic, authority-free projection to governing inputs
rationale: Front Door Basic must support a comprehensible human CLI (with a guided TUI as a later prospect) and a stable machine CLI/file interface for automation and later Level 1, both producing the same structured, validatable semantic Commission. A deterministic Commission projection derives the required governing inputs from it without making its own professional or authority-granting decisions, reusing the authority-free, provider-free projection role the Commissioning concept already assigns to a CommissionCompiler above the trust boundary. The operator must be able to see, before and after execution, which task, program revision, authority, and model bindings actually entered execution. The concrete schema shape and implementation decomposition are not designed by this decision.

title: Front Door Advanced is optional, deferred, and explicitly not the required interface between Level 1 and Level 0
rationale: Front Door Advanced -- a later, optional LLM-assisted producer of semantic Commissions -- remains post-MVP and unauthorized, consistent with the 2026-10-21 record's deferral of what it called Front Door Stage 2. This decision adds one explicit constraint the 2026-10-21 record did not state: Advanced is not the interface between Level 1 and Level 0. Level 1 must be able to submit already-planned, already-authorized work directly through the shared Commission contract (DEC-WFC-020); a mandatory LLM-commissioning hop between Level 1 and Level 0 execution must not become required for this. This narrows the 2026-10-21 record's Stage 2 direction, which described a WFC-controlled LLM Run authoring the real Commission as a plausible first Level-1 capability: that remains a legitimate optional convenience hypothesis, not a required path. Whether Advanced is useful at all as an optional convenience remains open.

title: Direct and Robust are the first reusable-program design targets, with Robust's renewed-broad-review-before-Complete invariant
rationale: Direct (a bounded worker task with no independent LLM review, but with whatever deterministic checks the task actually needs) and Robust (Implementation -> Broad Review; on a Finding, Correction and Focused Review; once Findings are closed, a renewed Broad Review before Complete) are selected as the first reusable-program design targets, as target requirements for a future design, not already-implemented or accepted programs. In the clean case Robust needs only Implementation and Broad Review; after any correction, no successful Completion may occur without a fresh full-breadth review, not merely a stronger final check. This loop is stricter than, and not yet expressible by, the base-pattern grammar hypothesis the 2026-10-26 Front Door boundary plan records (its twice-occurring WORK->GATE->WORK->GATE cycle does not yet name a gate-to-gate edge re-entering a broad review after a focused correction-check closes its Findings); this is recorded as a gap the eventual grammar must cover, not resolved here. Convergence Escape (FTR-WFC-CORRECTION-CONVERGENCE-ESCAPE, amended by Design Revision 001) is an extension worth investigating for Robust, not designed into it by this decision. Both programs must preserve unchanged: successor-Run continuation as a fresh, separately authorized Run (DEC-WFC-014); existing same-Run reconciliation; and the separation of salvage, authority, and continuation already canonical under DEC-WFC-013.

title: Archiving is a regular Front Door completion step with a configurable archive root preferring repository-local .wfc/archive/; run_ledger.adoc curation stays optional dogfooding, not a Beta-MVP requirement
rationale: Archiving becomes a normal, regular part of a completed Front Door run rather than a separate maintainer chore. The normal long-term archive location moves to a configurable root inside the consumer repository, preferably .wfc/archive/, sharpening the 2026-10-21 record's 'candidate hypothesis, nothing more' framing into a stated direction; the existing separate workflow-coordinator-run-evidence repository and its existing mechanical archiver (archive_run.py, delegated to by scripts/wfc_op.py archive) remain a fully supported alternative, not a legacy path to retire. The target audit trail carries Run/Attempt/Hop/Invocation identities and Git provenance, model/adapter/effective-permission bindings, review/Finding/routing/evidence outcomes, reported token-consumption data where available, and traceable association between WFC-generated commits and their executions. Run completion and the archive commit remain separate acts; the archive must not establish active runtime authority, carry secrets or unnecessary raw transcripts, or be agent-writable outside the archiver's protected path during execution; archiving a stopped Run and a repeated archive attempt must both work correctly. The curated run_ledger.adoc (operator manual section 11) remains useful dogfooding practice but is explicitly not a mandatory part of regular Beta-MVP operation; after the MVP only the mechanical evidence archive is required as the general audit trail. No archival schema, layout, or idempotency mechanics are designed by this decision.
